summary: God function (60+ lines, 8 responsibilities), no transaction boundary — payment/stock inconsistency risk. No tests.

findings.message: Payment charge (step 4) is committed before stock reduction (step 6). If stock reduction fails, the customer is charged but inventory stays intact — the DB is inconsistent.
findings.suggestion: Wrap steps 3-8 in a database transaction; either use a saga/outbox for the payment call or reserve stock BEFORE charging.

findings.message: process_checkout is 60+ lines with 8 distinct responsibilities (validate/coupon/tax/charge/persist/stock/email/clear). Untestable in units.
findings.suggestion: Extract validate_cart / apply_coupon / compute_tax / charge_payment / persist_order / reduce_stock / send_confirmation as separate functions.

findings.message: New checkout flow ships with zero tests. This is the highest-risk path in the system.
findings.suggestion: Add unit tests per extracted helper + an integration test covering the happy path + the payment-fails-mid-flight rollback path.
